anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet, LED1 is connected from +5V in series with C72 (2u2) to GND. There is no series current-limiting resistor in this path.
anomalies.expected: A steady power indicator should use a series current-limiting resistor. A capacitor in series blocks steady-state current and does not provide reliable LED current limiting.

evidence.quote: LED2 is shown with R8 240 in its indicator path (Power sheet, page 1/6)
5 V rail: A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V. (Power Section, §4)

anomalies.impact: LED1 will at most produce a transient flash as C72 charges, rather than indicate that the 5 V rail is present; the initial current pulse may also stress the LED.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present in the 5 V indicator circuit: LED1 is in series with a capacitor instead of a current-limiting resistor, so it will not provide a steady power indication.
